# How to Use This Guide

This is a master reference for the R/data skills covered across ISA 401 Classes
01, 02, 03, 04, 05, 06, 07, 08, 10, 11, and 12.

The main goal is not memorizing every line. You should be able to recognize
what a question is asking, choose the appropriate R function, and modify the
templates below.

---

# CLASS 01 — Business Intelligence / Data Visualization Foundations

## Big ideas

Know the basic progression:

1. Data
2. Information
3. Analysis
4. Insight
5. Decision/action

Be able to explain why business intelligence and data visualization help
organizations make better decisions.

## Basic R idea

R is a programming language used for data analysis, statistics, visualization,
and reproducible analytical work.

A typical analysis workflow is:

```{r}
# import data
data = readr::read_csv("data.csv")

# inspect data
dplyr::glimpse(data)

# transform data
result = data |>
  dplyr::filter(...) |>
  dplyr::group_by(...) |>
  dplyr::summarise(...)

# visualize/analyze result
result
```

## What to know

- What data analysis is doing
- Why reproducibility matters
- Why code is preferable to manually repeating transformations
- How R fits into a business analytics workflow

# CLASS 02 — Git Foundations

## Why Git?

Git tracks changes to files over time.

GitHub is a platform for storing/sharing Git repositories.

A repository is the project folder being tracked.

## Terms to recognize

| Term | Meaning |
|---|---|
| Repository | Project tracked by Git |
| Commit | Saved snapshot of changes |
| Push | Send local commits to GitHub |
| Pull | Bring remote changes to your computer |
| Clone | Copy a repository to your computer |
| Branch | Separate line of development |
| GitHub | Online hosting/collaboration platform |

## Reproducibility

A reproducible project allows another person to understand and recreate
the analysis.

Important habits:

- Keep code with the project
- Keep data organized
- Use relative paths when appropriate
- Commit meaningful changes
- Push work to the remote repository
- Avoid depending on undocumented manual steps

## Typical workflow

```text
Edit files
   ↓
Save
   ↓
Git status / review changes
   ↓
Commit
   ↓
Push
   ↓
GitHub contains updated project
```

# CLASS 03 — R FOUNDATIONS

# 1. Assignment

Use `<-` or `=` to assign a value.

```{r}
x = 10
y <- 20

x
y
```

## 2. Arithmetic

```{r}
10 + 5
10 - 5
10 * 5
10 / 5
10 ^ 2
10 %% 3
10 %/% 3
```

Know:

- `+` addition
- `-` subtraction
- `*` multiplication
- `/` division
- `^` exponent
- `%%` remainder
- `%/%` integer division

## 3. Variables

```{r}
price = 50
quantity = 4
revenue = price * quantity

revenue
```

## 4. Vectors

A vector contains multiple values.

```{r}
sales = c(100, 200, 300, 400)
sales
```

`c()` means combine.

```{r}
names = c("Joe", "Alex", "Sam")
```

## 5. Named vectors

```{r}
crashes_by_day = c(
  2020, 2241, 2327, 2285,
  2380, 1866, 1664
)

names(crashes_by_day) = c(
  "Mon", "Tue", "Wed", "Thu",
  "Fri", "Sat", "Sun"
)

crashes_by_day
```

Access by name:

```{r}
crashes_by_day["Wed"]
```

Access multiple names:

```{r}
crashes_by_day[c("Wed", "Fri")]
```

## 6. Comparisons

```{r}
crashes_by_day > 2100
```

This returns TRUE/FALSE for every value.

Other operators:

```{r}
x == 10
x != 10
x > 10
x < 10
x >= 10
x <= 10
```

IMPORTANT:

- `=` assigns
- `==` tests equality

## 7. Logical operators

```{r}
x > 10 & x < 20
x > 10 | x < 5
!(x > 10)
```

- `&` AND
- `|` OR
- `!` NOT

## 8. Data types

Common types:

- character
- numeric/double
- integer
- logical

```{r}
x = 10
typeof(x)
```

Character:

```{r}
x = "hello"
typeof(x)
```

Logical:

```{r}
x = TRUE
typeof(x)
```

Integer:

```{r}
x = 10L
typeof(x)
```

Example from class:

```{r}
crashes_per_day = 30125 / 365
crashes_per_day
```

## 9. Indexing

R starts counting at 1.

```{r}
sales = c(100, 200, 300, 400)

sales[1]
sales[2]
sales[1:3]
```

Named indexing:

```{r}
crashes_by_day[c("Wed", "Fri")]
```

Position indexing:

```{r}
crashes_by_day[c(3, 5)]
```

## 10. Sequences

```{r}
1:10
seq(from = 1, to = 10, by = 2)
```

## 11. Missing values

Missing values are represented by `NA`.

```{r}
x = c(10, 20, NA, 40)

is.na(x)
```

Many calculations need:

```{r}
mean(x, na.rm = TRUE)
```

## 12. Functions

General pattern:

```r
function_name(argument = value)
```

Examples:

```{r}
length(sales)
sum(sales)
mean(sales)
median(sales)
min(sales)
max(sales)
```

# CLASS 04 — DATA STRUCTURES / IMPORT

# 1. Vector

```{r}
x = c(10, 20, 30)
```

One-dimensional collection of values.

# 2. Matrix

```{r}
m = matrix(1:6, nrow = 2)
m
```

Two-dimensional structure where values generally have the same type.

# 3. List

Lists can contain different types and nested objects.

```{r}
job = list(
  title = "Research Data Scientist, Magic Eye",
  company = "Google",
  salary = list(
    min = 147000,
    max = 210000
  )
)
```

Access:

```{r}
job[[2]]
job$company
job$salary$max
job[[3]][[2]]
```

See names:

```{r}
names(job)
```

Important distinction:

```r
job[3]
```

returns a list.

```r
job[[3]]
```

returns the actual third element.

# 4. Data frame

A data frame is a table.

```{r}
df = data.frame(
  name = c("Joe", "Sam"),
  sales = c(100, 200)
)

df
```

Columns can be accessed with:

```{r}
df$name
df[["name"]]
df[, "name"]
```

Rows/columns:

```{r}
df[1, ]
df[, 1]
df[1, 1]
```

# 5. Subsetting

```{r}
sales = c(100, 200, 300, 400)

sales[1:3]
sales[c(1, 4)]
```

Logical subsetting:

```{r}
sales[sales > 200]
```

Named vector:

```{r}
crashes_by_day[c("Wed", "Fri")]
```

# 6. `glimpse()`

Use this constantly to understand a data frame.

```{r}
dplyr::glimpse(df)
```

It shows:

- number of rows
- number of columns
- column names
- column types
- sample values

# 7. CSV import

```{r}
data = readr::read_csv("data.csv")
```

Base R alternative:

```{r}
data = read.csv("data.csv")
```

# 8. Excel

```{r}
occupation = readxl::read_excel(
  path = "../data/occupation.xlsx",
  sheet = 5,
  skip = 1
)
```

Remove rows:

```{r}
occupation = occupation[-c(32, 33, 34), ]
```

Keep first 31:

```{r}
occupation = occupation[1:31, ]
```

```{r}

  "../data/midwest_airbnb.db"
```

```{r}
dplyr::glimpse(listings)
```

Remember:

```text
CONNECT → READ → WORK → DISCONNECT
```

# CLASS 07 — DATA WRANGLING WITH dplyr

This is one of the highest-value sections.

## The pipe

```r
data |>
  operation1() |>
  operation2()
```

Read it as:

> Take this data, then do this, then do this.

# 1. `select()`

Choose columns.

```{r}
listings |>
  dplyr::select(city, price, accommodates)
```

Rename while selecting:

```{r}
listings |>
  dplyr::select(
    city,
    nightly_price = price
  )
```

# 2. `filter()`

Keep rows meeting conditions.

```{r}
listings |>
  dplyr::filter(city == "Chicago")
```

Multiple conditions:

```{r}
listings |>
  dplyr::filter(
    room_type == "Entire home/apt" &
    accommodates >= 4
  )
```

OR:

```{r}
listings |>
  dplyr::filter(
    city == "Chicago" |
    city == "Columbus"
  )
```

# 3. `mutate()`

Create/change columns.

```{r}
listings |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    price_per_person = price / accommodates
  )
```

Multiple calculations:

```{r}
listings |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    revenue = price * accommodates,
    expensive = price > 200
  )
```

# 4. `arrange()`

Sort.

```{r}
listings |>
  dplyr::arrange(price)
```

Descending:

```{r}
listings |>
  dplyr::arrange(dplyr::desc(price))
```

# 5. `group_by()`

Creates groups for later summaries.

```{r}
listings |>
  dplyr::group_by(city)
```

Usually paired with `summarise()`.

# 6. `summarise()`

Create summary statistics.

```{r}
listings |>
  dplyr::group_by(city) |>
  dplyr::summarise(
    median_price = median(price)
  )
```

Count rows:

```{r}
listings |>
  dplyr::group_by(city) |>
  dplyr::summarise(
    count = dplyr::n()
  )
```

# 7. `n()`

Number of observations in the current group.

```{r}
listings |>
  dplyr::group_by(city) |>
  dplyr::summarise(
    count = dplyr::n()
  )
```

# 8. `count()`

Shortcut for counting groups.

```{r}
listings |>
  dplyr::count(city)
```

Sorted:

```{r}
listings |>
  dplyr::count(host_name, sort = TRUE)
```

# 9. `mean()`

```{r}
mean(listings$price)
```

Grouped:

```{r}
listings |>
  dplyr::group_by(city) |>
  dplyr::summarise(
    avg_price = mean(price, na.rm = TRUE)
  )
```

# 10. `median()`

```{r}
median(listings$price, na.rm = TRUE)
```

# 11. `across()`

Apply the same function to multiple columns.

```{r}
jobs |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    dplyr::across(
      dplyr::ends_with("_at"),
      as.Date
    )
  )
```

# 12. `bind_rows()`

Stack data frames vertically.

```{r}
final = dplyr::bind_rows(df1, df2, df3)
```

# 13. `head()`

```{r}
head(listings)
head(listings, 10)
```

# 14. `na.omit()`

Remove rows containing missing values.

```{r}
data |> na.omit()
```

## Class 07 complete examples

```{r}
con = DBI::dbConnect(
  RSQLite::SQLite(),
  "../data/scout.db"
)

postings = DBI::dbReadTable(
  con,
  "scout_postings"
) |>
  tibble::as_tibble()

DBI::dbDisconnect(con)

jobs = postings |>
  dplyr::select(
    company,
    title,
    location_state,
    remote,
    category,
    posted_at,
    last_seen_at
  ) |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    dplyr::across(
      dplyr::ends_with("_at"),
      as.Date
    ),
    days_open = as.numeric(
      last_seen_at - posted_at
    )
  )
```

Grouped summary:

```{r}
jobs |>
  dplyr::group_by(category) |>
  dplyr::summarise(
    postings = dplyr::n(),
    remote_share = mean(remote)
  )
```

Grouped by two variables:

```{r}
jobs |>
  dplyr::group_by(category, location_state) |>
  dplyr::summarise(
    postings = dplyr::n(),
    remote_share = mean(remote) |>
      round(digits = 2)
  ) |>
  dplyr::arrange(
    dplyr::desc(remote_share)
  ) |>
  na.omit()
```

Filter then group:

```{r}
jobs |>
  dplyr::filter(category == "fulltime") |>
  dplyr::group_by(location_state) |>
  dplyr::summarise(
    postings = dplyr::n(),
    remote_share = mean(remote) |>
      round(digits = 2)
  ) |>
  dplyr::arrange(
    dplyr::desc(remote_share)
  ) |>
  na.omit()
```

## Airbnb examples

```{r}
listings |>
  dplyr::group_by(city) |>
  dplyr::summarise(
    count = dplyr::n()
  )
```

Equivalent shortcut:

```{r}
listings |>
  dplyr::count(city)
```

Median price by city:

```{r}
listings |>
  dplyr::filter(
    room_type == "Entire home/apt" &
    accommodates >= 4
  ) |>
  dplyr::group_by(city) |>
  dplyr::summarise(
    median_price = median(price)
  ) -> q2

q2
```

Price per person:

```{r}
listings |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    price_per_person = price / accommodates
  ) |>
  dplyr::select(
    city,
    host_name,
    name,
    price,
    accommodates,
    price_per_person
  ) |>
  dplyr::arrange(price_per_person) |>
  head(3)
```

# CLASS 08 — APIs

## What is an API?

An API allows one program to request data/services from another system.

Typical flow:

```text
request
   ↓
URL + parameters + headers
   ↓
server
   ↓
response
   ↓
JSON
   ↓
R object/data frame
```

# 1. Basic `httr2` request

```{r}
httr2::request(
  "https://data.cincinnati-oh.gov/resource/rvmt-pkmq.json"
) |>
  httr2::req_url_query(
    "$limit" = 5
  ) |>
  httr2::req_perform() |>
  httr2::resp_body_string() |>
  jsonlite::fromJSON()
```

# 2. Query parameters

```{r}
req = httr2::request("https://example.com/api")

req |>
  httr2::req_url_query(
    parameter = "value"
  )
```

# 3. Headers

Some APIs require headers.

```{r}
httr2::request("https://example.com/api") |>
  httr2::req_headers(
    "User-Agent" = "your-email@example.com"
  )
```

# 4. Environment variables / API keys

Do NOT hard-code secret API keys.

```{r}
Sys.getenv("FRED_API_KEY")
```

Use:

```{r}
httr2::req_url_query(
  api_key = Sys.getenv("FRED_API_KEY")
)
```

# 5. FRED example

```{r}
ohio_jobs =
  httr2::request(
    "https://api.stlouisfed.org/fred/series/observations"
  ) |>
  httr2::req_url_query(
    series_id = "IHLIDXUSOH",
    api_key = Sys.getenv("FRED_API_KEY"),
    file_type = "json"
  ) |>
  httr2::req_perform() |>
  httr2::resp_body_string() |>
  jsonlite::fromJSON()

dplyr::glimpse(ohio_jobs)
```

Nested response:

```{r}
ohio_df = ohio_jobs$observations

dplyr::glimpse(ohio_df)
```

Dates:

```{r}
ohio_df |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    date = lubridate::ymd(date)
  ) |>
  dplyr::filter(
    date >= "2026-09-01"
  ) -> ohio_df_sept_2026
```

# 6. USAJobs API

```{r}
httr2::request(
  "https://data.usajobs.gov/api/search"
) |>
  httr2::req_url_query(
    Keyword = "Data Analyst",
    ResultsPerPage = 500
  ) |>
  httr2::req_headers(
    Host = "data.usajobs.gov",
    "User-Agent" = "fmegahed@miamioh.edu",
    "Authorization-Key" = Sys.getenv("USAJOBS_API_KEY")
  ) |>
  httr2::req_perform() |>
  httr2::resp_body_string() |>
  jsonlite::fromJSON(
    flatten = TRUE
  ) -> usa_jobs_data
```

Extract nested data:

```{r}
usa_jobs_df =
  usa_jobs_data$SearchResult$SearchResultItems
```

Select/rename:

```{r}
jobs_small = usa_jobs_df |>
  dplyr::select(
    title = MatchedObjectDescriptor.PositionTitle,
    department = MatchedObjectDescriptor.DepartmentName,
    agency = MatchedObjectDescriptor.OrganizationName,
    location = MatchedObjectDescriptor.PositionLocationDisplay,
    closes = MatchedObjectDescriptor.ApplicationCloseDate
  )
```

# 7. Search/count results

```{r}
jobs_small |>
  dplyr::count(department) |>
  dplyr::arrange(
    dplyr::desc(n)
  ) |>
  head(3)
```

# 8. String detection

Exact match:

```{r}
jobs_small |>
  dplyr::filter(
    title == "Data Analyst"
  )
```

Pattern match:

```{r}
index_data_analyst =
  jobs_small$title |>
  stringr::str_detect(
    "Data Analytics|Data Analyst"
  )

count_jesse_standard =
  jobs_small[index_data_analyst, ]
```

Then:

```{r}
count_jesse_standard |>
  dplyr::count(department) |>
  dplyr::arrange(
    dplyr::desc(n)
  )
```

# CLASS 10 — WEB SCRAPING

## What is web scraping?

Web scraping means programmatically retrieving information from a webpage.

Basic workflow:

```text
URL
 ↓
read_html()
 ↓
find HTML elements
 ↓
extract text/attributes/tables
 ↓
data frame
```

# 1. Check robots.txt

```{r}
robotstxt::paths_allowed(
  paths = "courses-instruction/isa/",
  domain = "https://bulletin.miamioh.edu/"
)
```

Another example:

```{r}
robotstxt::paths_allowed(
  paths = "/wiki/",
  domain = "https://en.wikipedia.org"
)
```

# 2. Read webpage

```{r}
page =
  rvest::read_html(
    "https://example.com"
  )
```

# 3. Find elements

```{r}
page |>
  rvest::html_elements("p")
```

CSS selector example:

```{r}
page |>
  rvest::html_elements(".courseblockdesc")
```

ID selector:

```r
"#some_id"
```

Class selector:

```r
".some_class"
```

Element selector:

```r
"p"
```

# 4. Extract text

```{r}
page |>
  rvest::html_elements("p") |>
  rvest::html_text2()
```

# 5. Extract one element

```{r}
page |>
  rvest::html_element("p")
```

# 6. Extract an attribute

```{r}
page |>
  rvest::html_element("a") |>
  rvest::html_attr("href")
```

# 7. Extract tables

```{r}
page |>
  rvest::html_elements("table") |>
  rvest::html_table()
```

## Miami course example

```{r}
isa_courses_in_r =
  rvest::read_html(
    "https://bulletin.miamioh.edu/courses-instruction/isa/"
  )

isa_courses_in_r |>
  rvest::html_elements(
    "#sc_sccoursedescs > div > p.courseblocktitle > strong"
  ) |>
  rvest::html_text2() ->
  isa_titles

isa_courses_in_r |>
  rvest::html_elements(
    ".courseblockdesc"
  ) |>
  rvest::html_text2() ->
  isa_desc

df = data.frame(
  title = isa_titles,
  description = isa_desc
)
```

## Key functions to recognize

```r
rvest::read_html()
rvest::html_elements()
rvest::html_element()
rvest::html_text2()
rvest::html_attr()
rvest::html_table()
```

# CLASS 11 — MULTI-PAGE SCRAPING

When one page is not enough, automate the repeated work.

# 1. Loop

```{r}
dept_abbrv =
  c("acc", "bus", "isa", "mkt")

courses_df = data.frame()

for (abbrv in dept_abbrv) {

  bulletin_url = paste0(
    "https://bulletin.miamioh.edu/courses-instruction/",
    abbrv,
    "/"
  )

  webpage =
    rvest::read_html(bulletin_url)

  webpage |>
    rvest::html_elements("strong") |>
    rvest::html_text2() ->
    titles

  webpage |>
    rvest::html_elements("p.courseblockdesc") |>
    rvest::html_text2() ->
    descs

  df = data.frame(
    title = titles,
    desc = descs
  )

  courses_df =
    rbind(courses_df, df)
}
```

# 2. Why `paste0()`?

It builds URLs dynamically.

```{r}
dept = "isa"

paste0(
  "https://bulletin.miamioh.edu/courses-instruction/",
  dept,
  "/"
)
```

# 3. Function

Instead of repeating code, create a function.

```{r}
scrape_mu_bulletin = function(abbrv) {

  bulletin_url = paste0(
    "https://bulletin.miamioh.edu/courses-instruction/",
    abbrv,
    "/"
  )

  webpage =
    rvest::read_html(bulletin_url)

  webpage |>
    rvest::html_elements("p.courseblocktitle") |>
    rvest::html_text2() ->
    titles

  webpage |>
    rvest::html_elements("p.courseblockdesc") |>
    rvest::html_text2() ->
    descs

  df = data.frame(
    title = titles,
    desc = descs
  )

  return(df)
}
```

Test:

```{r}
test =
  scrape_mu_bulletin(
    abbrv = "eco"
  )
```

# 4. `purrr::map_df()`

Apply the function to every department and combine rows.

```{r}
dept_abbrv =
  c("acc", "bus", "isa", "mkt")

courses_df_from_purrr =
  purrr::map_df(
    .x = dept_abbrv,
    .f = scrape_mu_bulletin
  )
```

Think:

```text
map_df =
run function on every item
+
combine outputs into one data frame
```

# CLASS 12 — STRUCTURED TEXT EXTRACTION / PAGINATION

# 1. Clean a scraped table

```{r}
year = 2025

crash_url =
  paste0(
    "https://www.planecrashinfo.com/",
    year,
    "/",
    year,
    ".htm"
  )

crash_page =
  rvest::read_html(
    crash_url,
    encoding = "ISO-8859-1"
  )

crash_tables =
  crash_page |>
  rvest::html_elements("table") |>
  rvest::html_table()

crash_df =
  crash_tables[[1]]

colnames(crash_df) =
  crash_df[1, ]

crash_df =
  crash_df[-1, ]

crash_df =
  crash_df |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    Date = lubridate::dmy(Date)
  )

head(crash_df)
```

# 2. Pagination

Suppose pages use:

```text
?start=1
?start=51
?start=101
...
```

Generate starting points:

```{r}
starts =
  seq(
    from = 1,
    to = 351,
    by = 50
  )
```

# 3. Preallocate a list

```{r}
pages =
  vector(
    "list",
    length(starts)
  )
```

A list is useful because each page produces a separate data frame.

# 4. Loop through pages

```{r}
base =
  "https://isa401-salvage.vercel.app"

starts =
  seq(
    from = 1,
    to = 351,
    by = 50
  )

pages =
  vector(
    "list",
    length(starts)
  )

for (i in seq_along(starts)) {

  pg =
    rvest::read_html(
      paste0(
        base,
        "/registry?start=",
        starts[i]
      )
    )

  pages[[i]] =
    data.frame(
      class =
        pg |>
        rvest::html_elements(
          "div > ul > li:nth-child(1) > span"
        ) |>
        rvest::html_text2(),

      value =
        pg |>
        rvest::html_elements(
          "span.salvage-value"
        ) |>
        rvest::html_text2() |>
        stringr::str_remove(" MCr")
    )

  Sys.sleep(1)
}
```

# 5. Combine pages

```{r}
registry =
  dplyr::bind_rows(pages)
```

# 6. Filter and convert

```{r}
Dreadnoughts_df =
  registry |>
  dplyr::filter(
    class == "Dreadnought"
  ) |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    value = as.numeric(value)
  )
```

Calculate total:

```{r}
sum(Dreadnoughts_df$value)
```

## Pagination pattern to memorize

```text
create page numbers
      ↓
create empty list
      ↓
loop through page numbers
      ↓
read page
      ↓
scrape page
      ↓
store data frame in list
      ↓
bind_rows()
```

# STRUCTURED EXTRACTION WITH ELLMER

The course also demonstrates using an LLM to turn unstructured text into a
specified structured object.

## Open a chat

```{r}
chat =
  ellmer::chat_openai(
    model = "gpt-5.6-luna",
    params = ellmer::params(
      reasoning_effort = "none"
    )
  )
```

## Scrape text first

```{r}
isa125_text =
  rvest::read_html(
    "https://bulletin.miamioh.edu/courses-instruction/isa/"
  ) |>
  rvest::html_elements(
    "#sc_sccoursedescs > div:nth-child(1)"
  ) |>
  rvest::html_text2()
```

## Define structured output

```{r}
course_info =
  chat$chat_structured(
    isa125_text,

    type =
      ellmer::type_object(

        name =
          ellmer::type_string(
            description =
              "Name of the course. For example, ISA 235. Information Technology and the Intelligent Enterprise. Do not include the parantheses for the credit hour and do not end with a period"
          ),

        description =
          ellmer::type_string(
            description =
              "The description of the course without the prereqs."
          ),

        prereqs =
          ellmer::type_string(
            "List the information after Prerequisite:"
          )
      )
  )
```

## Concept

Instead of asking the model for free-form text:

```text
"Tell me about this course."
```

you define the structure you want:

```text
name
description
prereqs
```

This is called structured extraction.

# EXAM / QUIZ RECOGNITION GUIDE

## "Keep only rows where..."

Use:

```r
dplyr::filter()
```

Example:

```r
data |>
  dplyr::filter(price > 100)
```

## "Keep only these columns..."

Use:

```r
dplyr::select()
```

## "Create a new column..."

Use:

```r
dplyr::mutate()
```

## "Sort..."

Use:

```r
dplyr::arrange()
```

Descending:

```r
dplyr::arrange(dplyr::desc(variable))
```

## "For each city/category/state..."

Usually:

```r
group_by(city)
```

## "Calculate average/median/count for each..."

Usually:

```r
group_by(...) |>
summarise(...)
```

## "Count observations by..."

Usually:

```r
count(variable)
```

## "Get data from JSON..."

Use:

```r
jsonlite::fromJSON()
```

## "Call an API..."

Look for:

```r
httr2::request()
httr2::req_url_query()
httr2::req_perform()
httr2::resp_body_string()
```

## "Scrape a webpage..."

Look for:

```r
rvest::read_html()
rvest::html_elements()
rvest::html_text2()
```

## "Get a link..."

Use:

```r
rvest::html_attr("href")
```

## "Get a table from a webpage..."

Use:

```r
rvest::html_table()
```

## "Repeat scraping across several departments..."

Use either:

```r
for (...)
```

or:

```r
purrr::map_df()
```

## "Repeat across pages..."

Usually:

```r
seq()
vector("list", ...)
for (...)
bind_rows()
```

## "Wait between requests..."

```r
Sys.sleep(1)
```

# COMMON R MISTAKES

## Mistake 1 — `=` vs `==`

Wrong for comparison:

```r
x = 10
```

That assigns.

Comparison:

```r
x == 10
```

## Mistake 2 — R starts at 1

```r
x = c("A", "B", "C")

x[1]
```

returns `"A"`.

## Mistake 3 — `[]` vs `[[]]`

For a list:

```r
job[3]
```

returns a list containing the third item.

```r
job[[3]]
```

returns the third item itself.

## Mistake 4 — Forgetting the pipe

Instead of:

```r
filter(data, ...)
```

you can use:

```r
data |>
  dplyr::filter(...)
```

## Mistake 5 — Forgetting `group_by()`

If asked for a result for every city:

```r
data |>
  dplyr::group_by(city) |>
  dplyr::summarise(...)
```

## Mistake 6 — Sorting the wrong direction

Ascending:

```r
arrange(x)
```

Descending:

```r
arrange(desc(x))
```

## Mistake 7 — Forgetting to disconnect SQLite

```r
DBI::dbDisconnect(con)
```

## Mistake 8 — Hard-coding API keys

Use:

```r
Sys.getenv("API_KEY")
```

instead.

## Mistake 9 — Scraping without checking the page structure

Always inspect:

```r
page
```

and identify the correct CSS selector.

## Mistake 10 — Scraping many pages without a pause

Use:

```r
Sys.sleep(1)
```

when appropriate.

# ONE-PAGE MEMORY SHEET

```r
# ASSIGN
x = 10

# VECTOR
x = c(1, 2, 3)

# INDEX
x[1]

# LIST
x = list(a = 1, b = 2)
x$b
x[[1]]

# DATA FRAME
df = data.frame(a = 1:3, b = 4:6)

# INSPECT
dplyr::glimpse(df)

# IMPORT
readr::read_csv("file.csv")
readxl::read_excel("file.xlsx")
jsonlite::fromJSON("file.json")

# SQLITE
con = DBI::dbConnect(RSQLite::SQLite(), "file.db")
df = DBI::dbReadTable(con, "table")
DBI::dbDisconnect(con)

# DPLYR
df |>
  dplyr::filter(x > 10) |>
  dplyr::select(a, b) |>
  dplyr::mutate(new = a + b) |>
  dplyr::group_by(a) |>
  dplyr::summarise(n = dplyr::n()) |>
  dplyr::arrange(dplyr::desc(n))

# API
httr2::request("URL") |>
  httr2::req_url_query(key = "value") |>
  httr2::req_perform() |>
  httr2::resp_body_string() |>
  jsonlite::fromJSON()

# SCRAPE
page = rvest::read_html("URL")

page |>
  rvest::html_elements("CSS_SELECTOR") |>
  rvest::html_text2()

# FUNCTION
f = function(x) {
  x * 2
}

# LOOP
for (i in 1:10) {
  print(i)
}

# MAP
purrr::map_df(items, f)

# MULTI-PAGE
starts = seq(1, 351, 50)
pages = vector("list", length(starts))

for (i in seq_along(starts)) {
  pages[[i]] = ...
  Sys.sleep(1)
}

result = dplyr::bind_rows(pages)
```

```{r}
    ".courseblockdesc"
  ) |>
  rvest::html_text2() ->
  isa_desc

df =
  data.frame(
    title = isa_titles,
    description = isa_desc
  )
```

## Class 11

```{r}
dept_abbrv =
  c("acc", "bus", "isa", "mkt")

scrape_mu_bulletin =
  function(abbrv) {

    bulletin_url =
      paste0(
        "https://bulletin.miamioh.edu/courses-instruction/",
        abbrv,
        "/"
      )

    webpage =
      rvest::read_html(
        bulletin_url
      )

    webpage |>
      rvest::html_elements(
        "p.courseblocktitle"
      ) |>
      rvest::html_text2() ->
      titles

    webpage |>
      rvest::html_elements(
        "p.courseblockdesc"
      ) |>
      rvest::html_text2() ->
      descs

    df =
      data.frame(
        title = titles,
        desc = descs
      )

    return(df)
  }

courses_df_from_purrr =
  purrr::map_df(
    .x = dept_abbrv,
    .f = scrape_mu_bulletin
  )
```

## Class 12

```{r}
starts =
  seq(
    from = 1,
    to = 351,
    by = 50
  )

pages =
  vector(
    "list",
    length(starts)
  )

for (i in seq_along(starts)) {

  pg =
    rvest::read_html(
      paste0(
        base,
        "/registry?start=",
        starts[i]
      )
    )

  pages[[i]] =
    data.frame(
      class =
        pg |>
        rvest::html_elements(
          "div > ul > li:nth-child(1) > span"
        ) |>
        rvest::html_text2(),

      value =
        pg |>
        rvest::html_elements(
          "span.salvage-value"
        ) |>
        rvest::html_text2() |>
        stringr::str_remove(" MCr")
    )

  Sys.sleep(1)
}

registry =
  dplyr::bind_rows(pages)
```
